approved: Universities Accord (National Higher Education Code to Prevent and Respond to Gender-based Violence) Bill 2025
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that creates a new regulatory system to reduce gender-based violence in higher education and make providers more accountable, including in student housing.

The minister would set a National Code with binding standards, and a new unit in the Department of Education would monitor compliance, with powers to investigate, issue notices and seek court penalties.
The bill also requires each provider's Vice-Chancellor or equivalent leader to be accountable for compliance and to report regularly to the governing body on incident data and prevention efforts.
Establishes a new regulatory framework for preventing and responding to gender-based violence in higher education.
Gives the minister power to make a National Code as a legislative instrument.
Creates a specialist gender-based violence unit within the Department of Education.
Gives the Secretary monitoring, investigation and enforcement powers including compliance notices, infringement notices and civil penalties.
Requires providers to develop a Gender Equality Action Plan and Gender Impact Assessments.
Requires providers to have trauma-informed policies and procedures and appropriately skilled staff.
Higher education providers, their staff and students, and the Department of Education.
